title: Comment on J.Qin et al., Unconditional and Robust Quantum Metrological Advantage beyond N00N States, PRL 130, 070801 (2023) and J.A. H. Nielsen et.al., Deterministic Quantum Phase Estimation beyond N00N States. PRL 130, 123603 (2023)
abstract: The papers by Qin et al. [1] and Nielsen et al. [2] report an unconditional quantum metrological advantage based on squeezed-vacuum phase sensing. The principal evidence for this claim is the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) evaluated per trial or per detected photon, which is subsequently interpreted as a measure of metrological performance. This interpretation is statistically unjustified because it does not account for the total experimental resources required to construct an estimator. Consequently, the reported protocols do not provide an unconditional metrological advantage over classical phase-sensing strategies when resource accounting is performed consistently.
summary: This theoretical paper challenges the notion of an unconditional quantum advantage in phase sensing using squeezed vacuum states. The authors argue that by failing to account for the total experimental resources, previous analyses overestimate the metrological gain. They demonstrate that proper resource accounting reduces the scaling advantage to match classical limits.
main_problem: The paper critiques the claim of an unconditional quantum metrological advantage reported by other studies using squeezed-vacuum phase sensing.
main_result: The reported advantage is statistically unjustified because the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) per trial fails to account for the total experimental resources required for accurate estimation.
method: The analysis relies on re-evaluating the resource scaling by consistently accounting for the total number of photons ($N$) rather than just the QFI per trial.
model_or_system: The discussion centers on quantum metrology applied to single-mode squeezed vacuum states used for phase sensing.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), total number of photons ($N$), and the achievable phase resolution $(\Delta\phi)^2$.
important_parameters: Squeezing parameter ($r$), number of repetitions ($n$), and the total resource $N = n ar{n}$.
main_assumptions: The critique focuses on the statistical interpretation of the results, assuming the underlying physical model of phase estimation is correct.
figures_summary: References are made to Figure 3(a), which reportedly shows calibration curves where statistical fluctuations are smaller than the symbol size.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by identifying the core claim, establishing the theoretical framework (Cramér–Rao inequality), developing the resource accounting critique, and concluding that the advantage vanishes upon proper resource normalization.
why_interesting: It provides a crucial methodological correction in quantum metrology, warning researchers against over-interpreting QFI as the sole measure of achievable precision.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
